To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the standard DOAS method is valid only for weak absorption, (2) the WFDOAS method is valid in the whole range of the absorption coefficient values, (3) the MDOAS method is also valid in the whole absorption range, but its application to observations of the scattered light is limited by a condition of weak scattering, and (4) in the general case of a weak absorption and a weak scattering, the WFDOAS and MDOAS methods are identical.

(i) The weighting function, which represents the differential optical absorption spectroscopy equation, is a function of all atmospheric parameters including the scattering coefficient, the absorption coefficient, and the solar zenith angle; (ii) the weighting function is not equal to the differential air mass factor, which is often used in the differential optical absorption spectrometry equation, and (iii) the standard differential optical absorption spectrometer equation is applicable only in the case of weak absorption, when the differential optical absorption equation is valid
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the DOAS analysis of the scattered light.

the development of a theoretical basis and a quantitative analysis of the applicability ranges of different forms of DOAS equation for the observations of the scattered light in the atmosphere and the light reflected from the Earth surface.
the theoretical investigation of the DOAS concept for multiply scattering media and the relationship between the weighting function and the air mass factor in the DOAS technique.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the standard DOAS method is applicable to the observations of both the direct and scattered solar light in those cases only where the contribution of multiple scattering processes is negligible.

the WFDOAS, MDOAS, and standard DOAS methods can be applied to retrieve the atmospheric species concentrations from the observations of the multiple scattered solar light in the atmosphere with the same accuracy and under the same conditions as the standard DOAS method is used for the observations of the directly transmitted solar light.
the standard DOAS approach is not valid for the observations of the scattered light if the contribution of the atmospheric multiple scattering is not negligible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WFDOAS and the MDOAS equations can be applied for the analysis of the scattered solar radiation with a non-niglible contribution of multiple scattering.
for the DOAS technique to be applicable the absorption coefficient of the atmospheric species under investigation has to be weak.

the DOAS method is a powerful tool for the determination of the air mass factor for the multiply scattering vertically in-homogeneous medium, and that the standard DOAS is applicable for the determination of air mass factors in a wide range of the atmospheric conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WFDOAS equation is the most general form of the standard DOAs equation.

the standard DOAS method is applicable for the retrieval of the amounts of atmospheric species only when the contribution of the gaseously induced absorption to the total optical thickness is much smaller than the contribution of the scattering.
the DOAS equation can have different forms depending on the specific problem under consideration.
